mechanism_narrative: A sustained low level of federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may lead to increased borrowing and investment, thus driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are not positively correlated with sustained low FEDFUNDS levels, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate suggests a weak labor market, which could lead to decreased consumer spending and negative impacts on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns despite high unemployment, this hypothesis is disproven.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing real sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which may lead to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth does not correlate with positive S&P 500 returns, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) suggests expansion in the construction sector and overall economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by 5% in one month
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but S&P 500 returns are negative, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates increased economic activity, which may boost corporate profits and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth does not predict positive S&P 500 returns, this hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) combined with falling employment (PAYEMS) indicates a weakening labor market, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls but S&P 500 returns are positive, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) may lead to decreased borrowing and investment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rise but S&P 500 returns are positive, this hypothesis is disproven.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) combined with high federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) may lead to decreased consumer and business spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If both CPIAUCSL rises and FEDFUNDS are high but S&P 500 returns are positive, this hypothesis fails.
